lunyx.title: Water ice-bearing permanently shaded regions (PSRs), lunar south polar region
lunyx.citation: Lemelin, M., Li, S., Mazarico, E., Siegler, M. A., Kring, D. A., & Paige, D. A. (2021). Database of water ice-bearing permanently shaded regions in the lunar south polar region [Data set]. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.4646092
lunyx.paper: Lemelin, M., et al. (2021). Framework for Coordinated Efforts in the Exploration of Volatiles in the South Polar Region of the Moon. Planetary Science Journal, 2, 103. https://doi.org/10.3847/PSJ/abf3c3
changes: Polygons from the shapefile; attributes from the .xls (blank cells kept as null; the DBF stores them as 0).
Reprojected from Moon2000 south-polar stereographic (sphere R = 1737400 m, true scale at the pole) to planetocentric lat/lon degrees (east-positive, -180..180) on the same sphere.
Ring vertices simplified with Douglas-Peucker at 30 m (projected); 33067 -> 4142 vertices; worst per-region area change 5.00%. Area_m2/Area_km2 are the authors' values, not recomputed.
Coordinates rounded to 1e-4 degree (<= 11 m). Feature ids "lemelin2021-psr-<FID>" added.
geometryNotes: Each feature is an AREA (polygon), not a point. Latitude/Longitude are the authors' "center" of the region, for labelling only; distances should be measured to the polygon.

The published outlines are larger than the listed PSR areas (Area_km2): the equivalent-circle difference is 282-529 m (median 312 m), consistent with region-of-interest outlines that extend ~0.3 km beyond each PSR. This is our inference; the record does not document it. A distance of 0 means inside the mapped outline, not necessarily inside the PSR.
FID 154 (Wiechert J): the listed centre is ~100 km from the polygon; flagged "center-outside-polygon". Use the polygon for position.
Polygons near the pole may span many longitudes; render per-vertex on the sphere, not on a flat lon/lat map.

units.MAX_illum_1km: fraction of time 0..1 (source text says 0-100%, stored values are 0..1)
units.MIN_dist_5deg: m (inferred; slope-limited traverse distance, null = no route under that slope)

columns.FID: ID of each water ice-bearing permanently shaded region (PSR) based on M3 detections
columns.Name: crater name if known
columns.Near_side: Is the PSR located on the near side (1) or not (0)
columns.Area_m2: Area of the PSR in squared meters
columns.Area_km2: Area of the PSR in squared kilometers
columns.Count_M3: Number of surficial water ice detections by M3 at the surface of the PSR
columns.M3_per_km2: Number of surficial water ice detections by M3 at the surface of the PSR divided by the Akea_km2
columns.Slope_access: Slope regime to be traveled on to access at least one M3 water ice detection from outside the PSR
columns.MIN_slope: Minimum slope value found within the PSR (at 120 meters per pixel)
columns.MAX_slope: Maximum slope value found within the PSR (at 120 meters per pixel)
columns.MEAN_slope: Mean slope value found within the PSR (at 120 meters per pixel)
columns.MIN_H: Minimum hydrogen value found within the PSR (from Lunar Prospector at 15 kilometers per pixel)
columns.MAX_H: Maximum hydrogen value found within the PSR (from Lunar Prospector at 15 kilometers per pixel)
columns.MEAN_H: Mean hydrogen value found within the PSR (from Lunar Prospector at 15 kilometers per pixel)
columns.Hydrogen_class: 1=0-50 ppm H, 2=50-100 ppm H, 3=100-150 ppm H, 4=150-200 ppm H (based on Mean_H)
columns.WEH_max_wt%: calculated using the pixon reconstructed Lunar Prospector Neutron Spectrometer hydrogen centent of Teodoro et al. (2010) and the equation of Lawrence et al. (2006)
columns.MIN_an_T: minimum annual bolometric temperatures derived from DIVINER at a spatial resolution of 240 meters per pixel (Paige et al. 2010)
columns.MAX_an_T: maximum annual bolometric temperatures derived from DIVINER at a spatial resolution of 240 meters per pixel (Paige et al. 2010)
columns.MEAN_T: mean annual bolometric temperatures derived from DIVINER at a spatial resolution of 240 meters per pixel (Paige et al. 2010)
columns.H2O_depth_min: minimum modeled stability of water ice (H2O) in the top meter of the regolith using DIVINER data and the method of Paige et al. (2010) and Siegler et al. (2016)
columns.H2O_depth_max: maximum modeled stability of water ice (H2O) in the top meter of the regolith using DIVINER data and the method of Paige et al. (2010) and Siegler et al. (2016)
columns.CO2_depth_min: minimum modeled stability of dry ice (CO2) in the top meter of the regolith using DIVINER data and the method of Paige et al. (2010) and Siegler et al. (2016)
columns.CO2_depth_max: maximum modeled stability of dry ice (CO2) in the top meter of the regolith using DIVINER data and the method of Paige et al. (2010) and Siegler et al. (2016)
columns.MAX_illum_1km: maximum proportion of time a pixel is illuminated within 1 km (euclidian distance of the PSR boundary) of the PSR (0-100%) based on the model of Mazarico et al. (2011) at 500 meters per pixel
columns.MAX_illum_5km: maximum proportion of time a pixel is illuminated within 5 km (euclidian distance of the PSR boundary) of the PSR (0-100%) based on the model of Mazarico et al. (2011) at 500 meters per pixel
columns.MAX_illum_10km: maximum proportion of time a pixel is illuminated within 10 km (euclidian distance of the PSR boundary) of the PSR (0-100%) based on the model of Mazarico et al. (2011) at 500 meters per pixel
columns.MIN_dist_5deg: minimum distance traveled between a potential landing site and an M3 water ice detection if traveling on slopes shallower than 5 degrees
columns.MIN_dist_10deg: minimum distance traveled between a potential landing site and an M3 water ice detection if traveling on slopes shallower than 10 degrees
columns.MIN_dist_15deg: minimum distance traveled between a potential landing site and an M3 water ice detection if traveling on slopes shallower than 15 degrees
columns.MIN_dist_20deg: minimum distance traveled between a potential landing site and an M3 water ice detection if traveling on slopes shallower than 20 degrees
columns.MIN_dist_25deg: minimum distance traveled between a potential landing site and an M3 water ice detection if traveling on slopes shallower than 25 degrees
columns.HIGHEST: Sites that would allow sampling the highest concentration of volatiles
columns.LATERAL: Sites best suited for characterizing the lateral distribution of water ice
columns.VERTICAL: Sites best suited for characterize the vertical distribution of volatiles
columns.FASTEST: Sites that would allow the fastest recovery of a scientifically interesting sample
columns.TOTAL_Obj: Number of objectives the site is best suited for (11 most promising PSRs = 2-4)
